newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha little moved, LSWR demand seen slack.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha little moved, LSWR demand seen slack.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were static in afternoon trading on Thursday, while the backwardation in inter-month spreads stayed wide due to tight near-term availability, traders said.
The one-month spread from second-half April was quoted little changed from Wednesday at plus $6.00/7.00.
Offers for second-half April open-spec naphtha were heard at $233.50 per tonne but no firm bids had surfaced. It was quoted at $233.00/234.00 in late trading on Wednesday.
First-half May was notionally assessed at $230.00/231.00, compared with Wednesday's $229.00/230.00.
Low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) trading for March cargoes is expected to get into full swing next week, traders said.
Premium levels for March-lifting Indonesian cargoes were assessed at about 70 cents per barrel over the Pertamina formula.

Demand from Japanese electric utilities, major end-users for imported LSWR, is expected to remain slow for the time being as the power firms usually try to keep their fuel oil inventories at the lowest possible levels toward the end of the business year, traders said. For most Japanese companies, the business year ends on March 31. --Tokyo Energy Desk
